recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Handle any future concern about a particular integer element through an artifact-specific Jira issue rather than reapplying FHIR-5654 globally.
issue_request: FHIR-5654 asked whether integer should be constrained to positive or non-negative values; the Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution retained integer and added unsigned/positive integer constraints with resource updates as appropriate.
initial_application: March 2015 commits a87257bf6bcf4f46ba484a2aa7683187d6bb1fbe and 963f5d8fac89aa18784f4a33882d7c069fb6255d added positiveInt/unsignedInt and applied #5654 to many then-current spreadsheets, including counts and sequence fields.
additional_context: Current datatypes.html and primitives.xml define signed integer, unsignedInt, and positiveInt; fhir.ini keeps the datatype pages and primitive metadata in build scope. Later decisions such as FHIR-16950, FHIR-19958, FHIR-25208, FHIR-41244, and FHIR-48399 explain current wording, integer64 use for Attachment.size, and retained valueInteger wording for Patient.multipleBirth.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because broad source edits are not needed and would risk conflicting with later artifact-specific decisions.
